newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean hospital workers lift strike.
newsitem.headline: Chilean hospital workers lift strike.

text.p: Chilean health workers voted Friday to lift a strike that had almost paralysed the country's public hospitals for 10 days, ending one of the most bitter labour challenges to President Eduardo Frei's government.
They lifted the strike without reaching an agreement on their wage demands but threatening to walk out again later if Frei's government did not meet at least part of their demands.
"As of midnight tonight, this strike is over, and we're going to keep fighting to make the government hear our demands," said union leader Guillermo Pena.
The Frei government, showing signs of getting tougher with Chile's increasingly assertive trade unions, declared the strike illegal and refused to negotiate with unions until they returned to work.
But the strike finally fizzled Thursday when hospital doctors decided not to join it.
The government made no concessions to end the strike except for a promise to study their demands, health ministry officials said.
Despite a prosperous economy, Chile has faced a series of labour stoppages in the public sector in the last few months, including by teachers and copper miners.
